title: Erdős 396 · central binomial and descending factorials
statement:
open Nat in
theorem erdos_396 : ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ n : ℕ, descFactorial n (k + 1) ∣ centralBinom n := by
  sorry
informal: For every k, is there an n such that n(n−1)⋯(n−k) divides the central binomial coefficient C(2n, n)?

formalConjectures.pinnedForm: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k, ∃ n, descFactorial n (k + 1) ∣ centralBinom n
formalConjectures.upstreamForm: ∀ k, ∃ n, descFactorial n (k + 1) ∣ centralBinom n

provenance.alphaproof: not attempted there: the comparison is against formal-conjectures and OEIS, not against an AlphaProof output

checks.compiledOn: Leak IV, only the expected sorry warning
comparisonLemmas: n = 2, 2480, 8178 satisfy the statement for k = 1, 2, 3 (kernel-checked)
k = 2: 2479 does not satisfy it, so 2480 is the least witness, as A375077 says

seeds:
open Finset Nat

/-- The formal statement's `descFactorial n (k+1)` is the product `n (n-1) ... (n-k)` of the informal problem and of OEIS A375077. -/
theorem descFactorial_is_the_product (n k : ℕ) :
    n.descFactorial (k + 1) = ∏ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), (n - i) :=
  Nat.descFactorial_eq_prod_range n (k + 1)

lemma cb_eq (n : ℕ) : n.centralBinom = (2 * n).descFactorial n / n ! := by
  rw [Nat.centralBinom_eq_two_mul_choose, Nat.choose_eq_descFactorial_div_factorial]

/-- The first three values of OEIS A375077 (smallest n for k = 1, 2, 3) satisfy the statement. -/
theorem E396_k1 : (2 : ℕ).descFactorial 2 ∣ (2 : ℕ).centralBinom := by
  rw [cb_eq]; decide +kernel

theorem E396_k2 : (2480 : ℕ).descFactorial 3 ∣ (2480 : ℕ).centralBinom := by
  rw [cb_eq]; decide +kernel

theorem E396_k3 : (8178 : ℕ).descFactorial 4 ∣ (8178 : ℕ).centralBinom := by
  rw [cb_eq]; decide +kernel

/-- Minimality for k = 2: the entry before 2480 does not work (A375077 says 2480 is the smallest). -/
theorem E396_k2_not_2479 : ¬ (2479 : ℕ).descFactorial 3 ∣ (2479 : ℕ).centralBinom := by
  rw [cb_eq]; decide +kernel
